info.name: Content Automation Platform — Manual Test Walkthrough
info.description:
Sequential, self-chaining walkthrough for every module implemented so far (all 12 planned OpenSpec changes): Auth, User Profile, Platform Catalogue (admin + public), Social Connections (LinkedIn + Facebook), Content Posts, Publishing & Execution, Retry, Premium Payment (bKash sandbox), Payment History, Upcoming Features (admin + premium user), and Admin Users/Audit Log. Run folders top to bottom, request by request, inside each folder. See docs/manual-testing-guide.md for the full step-by-step instructions and docs/credentials-setup-log.md for how the third-party credentials (Cloudinary, LinkedIn, Facebook, SMTP) were configured — this file is the companion collection to import.

Everything a later request needs (OTP, user id, platform id, session cookies) is captured automatically by each request's Tests script into collection variables — you never need to copy/paste a value by hand. The only things you might edit yourself are the `test_email`/`test_password` variables (Variables tab), and only if you're re-running the whole thing from scratch.

item.name: 01 - Auth
item.description: Registration, email verification, session, and password recovery. Run Register → Verify Email → Get Me first — that starts your session. Login / Refresh / Forgot / Reset are optional side-demos, safe to run any time after — they never end your session. Nothing here changes across re-runs except Register (see the guide's 'Re-running from scratch' section).

exec: console.log('409: this email is already registered. If it is already VERIFIED, skip the next request (Verify Email) and run "4. Login" instead, then continue from "3. Get Me".');

request.description:
Starts registration. Creates NO user row yet — just an OTP in Redis + (because EXPOSE_OTP_IN_RESPONSE=true in .env) the OTP in this response's `data.otp`, captured automatically into the `otp` variable for the next request.

Expected: 200 the first time. 409 means `test_email` already has a verified account — see the Tests script output in the Postman Console (View > Show Postman Console) for what to do next.

exec: console.log('Session cookies (accessToken/refreshToken) are now set — Postman will resend them automatically on every request below.');

request.description:
Completes registration using the `otp` captured by the previous request, creates the user, and logs you in (sets httpOnly `accessToken`/`refreshToken` cookies — Postman's cookie jar stores and resends these automatically on every request that follows, no manual header needed).

Expected: 201, with the created user in `data` (no password ever included). If this 400s with 'expired', the OTP is more than 5 minutes old — re-run '1. Register' to get a fresh one.

Confirms the session from step 2 works. Expected: 200 with your user profile. If you get 401 here, the cookies weren't sent — check Postman's cookie jar (bottom of the response panel > Cookies) has entries for localhost.

Only needed if you skipped Verify Email because your test_email was already verified (see Register's 409 note), or if you want to re-prove login works. Safe to run any time — just re-issues the same session cookies. Expected: 200.
Rotates the session using the httpOnly refreshToken cookie (sent automatically). Safe to run any time. Expected: 200.

Generates a password-reset code (captured into `reset_otp`). Always returns the same generic message whether or not the email exists (no account enumeration) — that's expected, not a bug. Does NOT touch your current session; safe to run any time.

exec: console.log('test_password variable updated to match the new password.');

request.description: Uses the `reset_otp` from the previous request to set a new password. Run '6. (Optional) Forgot Password' immediately before this one (the code expires in 5 minutes). Does NOT end your current session (cookies untouched) — safe mid-flow. After this runs, the `test_password` variable is auto-updated so every later request that logs in again keeps working.

item.name: 03 - Platform Catalogue (Admin)
item.description:
⚠️ SETUP REQUIRED FIRST — these routes need an ADMIN. There's no admin-signup API yet, so promote your test user directly:

1. Make sure the app's Postgres + Redis are running and `npm run dev` is up.
2. In a terminal, from the content-automation-backend folder, run:
   npm run admin:promote -- <the value currently in your test_email variable>
   (default is: npm run admin:promote -- postman.tester@example.com)
3. You should see 'Promoted <email> to ADMIN.' — checkAuth re-reads the role from Postgres on every request, so your EXISTING session cookies (from 01 - Auth) immediately count as admin. No re-login needed.

Run 01 - Auth and the promote command before anything in this folder.

exec: console.log('403 = your test_email is not ADMIN yet. Run the npm run admin:promote command in this folder\'s description first.');

item.name: 04 - Platform Catalogue (Public)
item.description: Requires only a logged-in session (any role) — run 01 - Auth first. Best run AFTER '03 - Platform Catalogue (Admin)' so you can see your retired test platform correctly excluded.

item.name: 05 - Social Connections
item.description:
Requires an active session — run 01 - Auth first.

✅ Real LinkedIn OAuth credentials are configured for this project (see docs/credentials-setup-log.md) and verified end-to-end — opening the authUrl from request 2 in a real browser and clicking Allow genuinely connects your account. ⏳ Facebook credentials are also configured (App ID/Secret + redirect URI), but the app's Page permissions (`pages_manage_posts`, `pages_read_engagement`) are still being finished on Facebook's side — see folder 05b.

What you can verify by hand below regardless: the endpoints exist, are session-guarded, gate on LIVE platforms, issue an OAuth URL + anti-forgery state, reject a forged callback, and enforce ownership on disconnect. The token encryption / storage / Page-selection behavior is also fully covered by the automated suite (tests/e2e/social-connections.e2e.test.ts).

request.description: Expected: 200 with an array (empty on a fresh account — you haven't connected anything). Tokens are NEVER included in this response by design.

Expected: 200 with `data.authUrl` — the LinkedIn OAuth URL (contains a `state=` anti-forgery token this server just issued into Redis). `linkedin` is a LIVE seeded platform, so connect is allowed.

✅ Real LINKEDIN_CLIENT_ID/SECRET are configured — copy `data.authUrl` into a real browser (logged into LinkedIn) and click Allow to genuinely connect your account. After the redirect back to localhost, re-run '1. List My Connections' above and you'll see a real row with your LinkedIn display name and a token expiry ~2 months out.

item.name: 3. Start Connect on a non-LIVE platform (refused)

request.description: Expected: 404 (no such platform). To see the 'not LIVE' 400 path instead, first create a COMING_SOON platform via 03 - Platform Catalogue (Admin) ▸ Create Platform with `"status": "COMING_SOON"`, then call `/connections/<that key>/connect` — it returns 400 because only LIVE platforms are connectable.

Expected: 400 — the OAuth callback validates the single-use `state` against Redis and refuses a value it never issued, storing nothing. This is the CSRF defense; a real provider redirect carries a state this server minted in step 2.
Expected: 404 if you never completed a real LinkedIn connect above, or 200 (hard-deletes the connection, physically removing the encrypted tokens) if you did.

item.name: 05b - Social Connections (Facebook)
item.description: Same session requirement as 05. Split out because Facebook's connect is a two-step flow (user token → pick a Page) that needs a real browser redirect, unlike LinkedIn's single step.

request.description:
Expected: 200 with `data.authUrl` — the Facebook OAuth dialog URL (contains a `state=` anti-forgery token). `facebook` is a LIVE seeded platform, so connect is allowed.

⏳ Real FACEBOOK_APP_ID/SECRET are configured, but the app's `pages_manage_posts`/`pages_read_engagement` permissions are still being finished on Facebook's side (see docs/credentials-setup-log.md) — opening this URL currently shows Facebook's 'Invalid Scopes' developer-only error instead of a real consent screen. Once resolved, opening it in a browser (logged into an account that administers a Facebook Page) shows a Page-picker if you administer more than one, or auto-selects if you only have one.

Only meaningful right after a real browser redirect from request 1 leaves a Page-selection stash in Redis. Expected: 200 with the Pages you administer (no tokens), or 400 ('No Facebook Page selection in progress') if you call it cold, as you would here without completing request 1 in a browser first.

Stores the chosen Page's token as the connection (encrypted) and clears the transient stash. Only meaningful right after request 2 actually returned Pages. Expected: 200 with the new connection, or 400 if there's no selection in progress or the pageId isn't among the held Pages.

item.name: 06 - Content Posts
item.description:
Requires an active session — run 01 - Auth (Register → Verify Email → Get Me) first. This is the content CRUD you asked to verify (OpenSpec change: add-content-posts): create a post (text + one optional image), list with pagination + search, get one, soft-delete, and confirm posts are immutable.

Run 1 → 10 in order. Everything a later request needs (the created post id) is captured automatically into the `post_id` variable — no copy/paste.

⚠️ What's fully checkable by hand here: create (text-only), list + meta, search, get-by-id, empty-content rejection, no-edit-endpoint (immutability), soft-delete, and gone-after-delete. The live IMAGE upload (request 3) needs real CLOUDINARY_* creds — this repo's .env has them empty (same as avatar/logo), so that one request is OPTIONAL and will 500 without them; that's expected, not a bug. Cross-user isolation (one user can't read or delete another's posts) can't be shown with a single session — it's proven by the automated suite (tests/e2e/content-posts.e2e.test.ts).

exec: pm.test('No image on a text-only post', function () {

request.description:
Creates a text post with no image. The body here is JSON — the endpoint accepts either JSON or multipart/form-data; you only need multipart when you're actually attaching an image (request 3).

Expected: 201. `data.imageUrl`/`data.imagePublicId` are null, `data.isDeleted` is false, and `data.userId` is you. The Tests script saves `data.id` into the `post_id` variable for every request below.
A second post whose content contains the word 'unicorns', so request 5 (Search) has a deterministic hit and request 4 (List) shows a total of at least 2. Expected: 201.

Owner-scoped list of your non-deleted posts. Expected: 200 with `data` (an array) and `meta` = { page, limit, total, totalPages }. After requests 1–2 the total is at least 2. Only YOUR posts appear — never another user's (that isolation is asserted by the automated suite).

Tweak `page`/`limit` and add `&sort=title` or `&sort=-createdAt` to see sorting; `-` prefix = descending.

request.description: Case-insensitive search over content + title. Expected: 200, and at least the post you created in request 2 ('unicorns are magical …') comes back. Search is combined with the same pagination/meta as request 4.

exec: pm.test('Returns the post captured in request 1', function () {

request.description: Fetch the single post you created in request 1 (via the captured `post_id`). Expected: 200, `data.id` equals `post_id`. A post id you don't own returns 404 and reveals nothing — that owner-scoping is covered by the automated suite.
Proves the non-empty-content rule. Whitespace-only content is trimmed to empty and rejected before anything is stored. Expected: 400, and no post is created.

exec: pm.test('No edit route exists (404)', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(404); });

request.description: Posts are immutable by design (spec: 'Posts are immutable after creation') so publishing history stays faithful — there is deliberately NO PATCH or PUT route on a post. Expected: 404 (route not found). Try the same URL with PUT if you like — same 404.

Soft-deletes the post from request 1: it's marked deleted and removed from your list, but the row is retained so publishing history that references it stays readable. Expected: 200. You can only delete your own post — deleting someone else's returns 404 (automated suite).

item.name: 10. Confirm Soft-Delete — Now 404 & Gone From List

exec: pm.test('Deleted post no longer retrievable (404)', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(404); });
console.log('Re-run request 4 (List) — the total dropped by one; the row still exists in the DB (soft delete), just hidden.');

request.description: The post you just soft-deleted is no longer retrievable. Expected: 404. Re-run request 4 (List My Posts) and you'll see the total dropped by one and this post gone from the array — while the underlying row is retained in Postgres (soft delete). That retention is asserted directly by the automated suite.

item.name: 07 - Publishing & Execution

request.description:
Kicks off a background publish of `post_id` to the given platform key(s). The platform must be LIVE **and** you must have a social connection for it (folder 05). Without a connection the service refuses (400).

Expected on success: 202 Accepted with `data.executionId` and `data.status = PENDING`. The Tests script saves `data.executionId` into `execution_id`. Real posting to LinkedIn/Facebook only happens if you completed real OAuth; otherwise the execution will move to FAILED — inspect it in the next requests.

Owner-scoped publish history, newest first, paginated. Filter with `?status=PENDING|RUNNING|COMPLETED|PARTIALLY_COMPLETED|FAILED` (the overall execution status — each platform's own result inside one execution is SUCCESS/FAILED, see the detail request below) and `?dateFrom=&dateTo=`.

Expected: 200 with `data` array + `meta` pagination.

Full detail for one execution: the published content plus each platform's `status`, `externalPostUrl` on success, the latest sanitized failure reason, and a `retryable` flag. The Tests script captures the first FAILED (or first) publication's id into `publication_id` for the retry folder.

Expected: 200.

exec: var target = pubs.find(function (p) { return p.status === 'FAILED'; }) || pubs[0];

item.description: Trigger a publish and read its history. Needs a post (folder 06) and, for real publishing, a live connection (folder 05).

item.name: 08 - Retry a Failed Publish

request.description:
Retries a single FAILED publication (id captured in folder 07 req 3). Only FAILED ones are retryable — retrying a SUCCESS one returns 400/409.

Expected: 202 Accepted (worker re-runs it in the background).

Retries every FAILED publication in the execution at once. If none are failed, returns 400 ('no failed publications to retry').

Expected: 202 Accepted.

item.description: Retry endpoints. Only meaningful after an execution has FAILED publications.

item.name: 09 - Premium Payment (bKash sandbox)

request.description:
Starts a bKash SANDBOX payment for the premium upgrade. Amount/currency come from server config — you send no body.

Expected: 201 with `data.paymentId` (your **local** payment row id — the only id you ever need; the bKash gateway's own session id is stored server-side and never returned to the client) and `data.redirectUrl` (open this in a browser to complete the sandbox payment). The Tests script captures `data.paymentId` into `payment_id` automatically — nothing to paste by hand. NOTE: needs valid BKASH_* sandbox creds in `.env`; without them this returns a gateway error.

exec: console.log('Open this URL in a browser to complete the sandbox payment:', d.redirectUrl);

request.description:
Idempotent server-side re-verification. `paymentId` is auto-filled from the `payment_id` variable captured in request 1 — nothing to paste. On a completed sandbox payment this flips `user.isPremium` true.

Expected: 200. Backend is authoritative — premium is only granted after the gateway itself confirms success (never trusts a client-supplied status).

Owner-scoped status of one payment row.

Expected: 200 with `data.status` (PENDING → SUCCESS once verified; FAILED or CANCELLED on a failed/cancelled sandbox payment).

item.description: bKash tokenized SANDBOX (test money). The browser-redirect callback (`GET /payments/callback`) is called by bKash, not you — it redirects to the frontend success/failure page, so it isn't a Postman request.

request.description:

Expected: 200 (safe projection) / 404 if missing.

item.name: 14 - Cleanup (optional — run at most ONE, LAST)
item.description:
⚠️ These are two ALTERNATIVE endings, not a sequence — run at most one, only once you're completely done testing everything above:

• '1. Delete My Account' — ends the session AND soft-deletes the user (it clears cookies itself as a side effect, so it must come first in this folder's order if you ever run both).
• '2. Logout' — ends the session only, keeps the user for later. Running this FIRST would make Delete My Account 401 (no session left) — that's why Logout is listed second here, as a fallback if you decide not to delete.

Most of the time you'll run neither and just leave your test data in place for next time.

request.description: Soft-deletes your test user and clears the session cookies as a side effect (no separate Logout needed after this). Expected: 200. After this, `test_email` can never `Register` fresh again (the row still exists, just soft-deleted) — pick a new `test_email` (Variables tab) if you want to run this whole collection again from scratch.

Only run this if you did NOT run '1. Delete My Account' (that request already clears cookies). Clears your session cookies, keeps the user/account intact for a future run. Expected: 200. Re-run '4. (Optional) Login' under 01 - Auth if you want to keep testing afterward.
